relations.subject: tool:cbimport
relations.evidence: This tool supports authenticating against a Couchbase Cluster by using certificate based authentication (mTLS authentication).

relations.subject: tool:cbimport
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate ('the subject's behaviour is influenced by the object setting or surface, without the setting being a hard prerequisite') - key generation is optional per the OPTIONS table
relations.evidence: The cbimport command also supports custom key-generation for each document in the imported file. Key generation is done with a combination of pre-existing fields in a document and custom generator functions supplied by cbimport.

relations.subject: tool:cbimport
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted, same predicate as the key-generator relation above
relations.evidence: When importing to a collection aware cluster you may optionally choose to provide a scope/collection expression which will be used to determine which scope/collection to insert the imported document in.

notable_absence.finding: Neither the REQUIRED nor OPTIONAL flag tables state which RBAC role/privilege the -u/--username account must hold; the page only says generically 'The user must have the appropriate privileges to import data.' Contrast with learn/security/roles.md's 56 named roles elsewhere in the corpus - this page never names one, so no requiresServerRole relation could be minted here without inventing the role name.

cross_component_finding: DISCUSSION states 'While importing CSV the cbimport command only utilizes a single reader. As a result importing large dataset may benefit from being partitioned into multiple files and running a separate cbimport process on each file' - a scaling recommendation with no named mechanism (no flag, no concept) to attach it to; recorded here rather than forced onto -t/--threads, which controls write-side concurrency to the cluster, not the read-side single-reader limitation this sentence describes. Those are two different bottlenecks on the same command and the page does not conflate them, so this record does not either.
